openings.claim: Clamp closure may disturb datum seating; elastic preload during closure could preserve the insertion position.
openings.delta: Attack the dependence on seating surviving movable-plate tightening. Keep the incumbent pockets, stops and captive hardware; add a supplied elastic loop per pocket, arranged to bias its rod toward the corner and insertion stop while the operator closes the clamp. Remove preload before checking return so elastic restraint cannot mask failure.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: pocket compliance, rather than seating disturbance, explains poor return. Closure-induced pointer movement that decreases with preload, followed by similar loaded deflection, favors disturbed seating. Comparable closure movement or return scatter defeats this branch; equal excessive loaded drift favors inadequate pocket stiffness. These predictions are unverified.
openings.probe: Build one configuration within 100 minutes, first checking 90 mm envelope, hand-only operation and cord-retained hardware. Within twenty minutes perform twelve exchanges, six per rod position, alternating ordinary seating and elastic-preloaded closure; use the 18 mm rod for the last two exchanges of the smaller position. Record pointer position immediately before and after tightening, then after removing preload, and exchange duration. Apply four ten-second 10 N loads across both procedures and rod sizes. Check every final return and loaded position against the 2 mm circle; fail any forty-second exchange or freed component. This is a diagnostic probe, with only three exchanges per procedure per rod, not independent complete validation of both procedures.
assumptions: Incumbent pocket geometry fits six plywood pieces and eight bolts; no extra hardware is available.
Loops can supply directional preload inside the envelope without obstructing exchange or leaving a permanent rod mark.
Ruler and target permit useful closure-shift measurements; precision and plywood stiffness remain unknown.

attacks.dependency: Datum seating remains unchanged while the movable clamp plate tightens.

assessment: One constructive dependency attack produces an executable comparison if the incumbent geometry and loop routing pass fabrication checks. Capacity or measurement failure defeats this probe; no deployment performance is established.

lineage.reason: Retains datum-and-stop positioning while testing whether transient elastic preload prevents clamp-induced reseating.
